targetReport.title: Local Government Act (Cap. 22:01), Malawi
targetReport.publisher: Government of Malawi / Parliament of Malawi
targetReport.description: Malawi's organic local government law, verified via the MalawiLII/Laws.Africa consolidated text (as at 2017-12-31). Sec. 79(1): "In every financial year a rate shall be made and levied by the Council to meet some liabilities falling to be discharged out of the general fund," with Sec. 79(4) allowing the council to differentiate rates "between areas and between classes of property." Sec. 44(1): "The sources of revenue for the Council to finance its operations shall be those stated in the Third Schedule." targetReport.title: Loi n°2017-051 du 02 octobre 2017 portant Code des Collectivités Territoriales (ABROGÉE par la Loi n°2023-004)
targetReport.publisher: Présidence de la République du Mali
targetReport.description: The predecessor collectivités code, verified via a FAOLEX mirror of the Journal Officiel text (06 October 2017), promulgated by then-President Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta. Art. 28 creates FNACT: "L'Etat garantit et organise le principe de solidarité entre les Collectivités territoriales. Il est créé à cet effet un Fonds national d'Appui aux Collectivités territoriales (FNACT)." Art. 29 sets an explicit numeric transfer floor and a natural-resource retrocession clause: "L'Etat procède annuellement à un transfert des ressources budgétaires aux Collectivités territoriales. Le taux de transfert qui ne peut être inférieur à 30% en 2018...sont définies par la loi de finances. L'Etat rétrocède aux Collectivités territoriales concernées un pourcentage des revenus issus de l'exploitation, sur leur territoire, des ressources naturelles." This is the clearest verbatim primary-source statement found in this branch's Mali research establishing both FNACT's legal creation and a hard minimum transfer rate. It is no longer in force, expressly abrogated by Art. 251 of ml-loi-2023-004-code-collectivites — kept in the corpus as a historical/superseded citation documenting the specificity the current code dropped.
targetReport.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument, no longer in force (superseded 2023).

targetReport.title: Loi n° 2013-10 du 28 décembre 2013 portant Code général des Collectivités locales (Acte 3 de la décentralisation)
targetReport.publisher: Assemblée Nationale du Sénégal / la Primature
targetReport.description: Senegal's 2013 decentralization reform code, verified via direct download of the official Primature (Prime Minister's office) PDF, cross-checked against an independent mirror. Art. 185 (own-source revenue): lists direct communal taxes ("taxe sur la valeur des locaux servant à l'exercice d'une profession; taxe d'enlèvement des ordures ménagères; taxe de balayage...") and indirect communal taxes ("taxe sur l'électricité consommée; taxe sur l'eau; taxe sur la publicité;...taxe sur les distributions d'essence, de gas-oil"), with rate-setting delegated to municipal council deliberation within nationally-fixed maxima. Art. 281: "Les ressources nécessaires à l'exercice par les collectivités locales de leurs compétences leur sont dévolues soit par transferts de fiscalité, soit par dotations, ou par les deux à la fois." KEY FINDING — Art. 324 creates the Fonds de Dotation de la Décentralisation (FDD): "Le fonds de dotation de la décentralisation, créé par la loi des finances, reçoit une dotation équivalant à 3,5% de la Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée perçue au profit du budget de l'Etat." Art. 328 creates the Fonds d'Équipement des Collectivités locales (FECL): "reçoit une dotation équivalant à 2% de la Taxe sur la Valeur ajoutée...réparti sur la base du principe de la solidarité nationale, chaque année, par arrêté conjoint du Ministre chargé des Finances et du Ministre chargé des Collectivités locales." Both percentages are stated as floors, revisable only upward: "Ce pourcentage est modifié dans le sens d'une hausse progressive, à chaque fois que de besoin."
targetReport.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument, amended 2019 (this article set confirmed unchanged).

results.basis: The MRF Guidelines state that Alberta Energy determines a well's monthly revenue by 'multiplying volumes of all the hydrocarbons produced, including test production, by their respective par/reference prices as published in the Information Letters available on the Alberta Energy website' (Revenue = Production * Par Price), and that 'the price component of oil is determined by using the monthly oil par price (PP) based on density'. The rate brackets are literal par-price thresholds: PP <= 251.70, 251.70 < PP <= 409.02, 409.02 < PP <= 723.64, 723.64 < PP. The Petroleum Royalty Regulation, 2017 s.5 gives the Minister the power to 'determine an amount per cubic metre as the par price' for light, medium, heavy and ultra-heavy oil, and its Schedule sets rp% = [(par price - 251.70) x ...].

However, the degree of alignment able to be achieved is sometimes adversely affected by competing classification principles e.g. a different organisation or structure of Australian or New Zealand industry, or a lack of significance of some internationally recognised economic activities in the two economies." The parentage is stated for the predecessors too: the 1969 ASIC "was based at the broader levels on the ISIC", the 1970 NZSIC was "based on ISIC, Rev.2", and the driver for a single joint classification was "the need to update each country's classifications to align with ISIC, Rev.3 issued in 1990." targetReport.title: International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC)
targetReport.description: The United Nations' industry classification and the acknowledged parent of most national industrial classifications, including ANZSIC and its two predecessors. Its absence from this corpus was a hole of the same shape as the missing `gasb-standards` that the associated-states pass had to fill: `naics` was present with eight inbound edges while the classification NAICS itself is aligned to was not represented at all. Adopted 1948; revisions 1 (1958), 2 (1968), 3 (1990), 3.1 (2002), 4 (2007) and 5 (endorsed 2023, publication forthcoming).
targetReport.cadence_note: Six revisions in seventy-five years. Rev. 5 was endorsed by the UN Statistical Commission at its 54th session in 2023 and, as of this session's read of the UNSD page, is 'forthcoming' in published form while being distributed as introduction, explanatory notes and structure files. releases_per_year is nominal.

release_schedule.note: ISIC has no publication calendar or fixed revision cycle. Revisions occur irregularly and infrequently (Rev.3: 1989, Rev.3.1: 2002, Rev.4: 2008, Rev.5: endorsed by the UN Statistical Commission at its 54th session in March 2023). National adaptation of Rev.5 is targeted by 2025, business register updates by 2026, and statistical program implementation from 2027, but these are implementation milestones for the already-published Rev.5, not a future release date. The UN Committee of Experts on International Statistical Classifications recommended a five-year revision cycle for ISIC/CPC (raised at the 55th Statistical Commission session, 2024), but as of the 56th session (2025) documents, this had not been formally adopted -- a new Standing Task Team on ISIC and CPC was instead tasked with developing a revision-cycle strategy proposal. No computable next revision date exists yet.

targetReport.title: Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC)
targetReport.publisher: Australian Bureau of Statistics and Statistics New Zealand (Tatauranga Aotearoa)
targetReport.description: The single industry classification used by both Australian and New Zealand official statistics, and the structural twin of `naics` — a classification agreed and maintained jointly by the statistical agencies of more than one country, from which each publishes national statistics. Its Preface is signed by both national statisticians: "Dennis Trewin / Brian Pink — Australian Statistician / Government Statistician — Australian Bureau of Statistics, Statistics New Zealand". Catalogue no. 1292.0; hierarchical, four levels (Division, Subdivision, Group, Class), 19 divisions and 86 subdivisions in the 2006 edition. Replaced two separate national classifications, the Australian Standard Industrial Classification (ASIC, 1969/1978/1983) and the New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (NZSIC, 1970/1975/1987), both of which were themselves derived from ISIC.
targetReport.cadence_note: Two editions in thirty-plus years — 1993 and 2006 — with a Revision 1.0 (Feb 2006) and Revision 2.0 (26 June 2013) of the 2006 edition. Next release listed by the ABS as 'Unknown'. Not an annual release; releases_per_year is nominal, and deliberately lower than `naics`'s 0.2 because ANZSIC has no five-year cycle.

release_schedule.note: ANZSIC is a joint ABS/Stats NZ industry classification standard revised only as needed, not on a fixed cycle. History: ANZSIC 1993 (original), ANZSIC 2006 Revision 1.0, ANZSIC 2006 Revision 2.0 (released 26 June 2013). The ABS 'latest-release' page itself lists 'Next release: Unknown'. No stated rule or calendar for a future revision was found; the ANZSCO (occupation) classification has an active comprehensive review underway, but that is a separate standard from ANZSIC (industry).

targetReport.title: Canada Health Transfer
targetReport.description: The largest major federal transfer to provinces and territories, providing federal cash support for health care and backing the criteria of the Canada Health Act. The national cash contribution is set in statute at section 24.1 of the Federal-Provincial Fiscal Arrangements Act and escalates each year by a three-year moving average of nominal GDP growth subject to a 3 per cent floor; the national amount is then divided among provinces on an equal per capita basis under section 24.21. Finance Canada publishes provincial and territorial entitlement amounts each year before the start of the fiscal year.
targetReport.cadence_note: The escalator must be determined by the Minister of Finance not later than three months before the beginning of the fiscal year, i.e. by the end of December for the fiscal year starting the following April 1. Entitlements are re-estimated several times during and after the year under the CHT/CST Regulations, but there is one authoritative annual determination.

However, a consistent annual pattern exists: the Minister/Deputy PM issues a news release in mid-to-late December each year announcing preliminary major federal transfer amounts (including CHT) for the fiscal year beginning the following April. Confirmed instances: Dec 2021 (for 2022-23), Dec 2022 (for 2023-24), Dec 15 2023 (for 2024-25), Dec 23 2024 (for 2025-26), and the major-federal-transfers.html table was updated Dec 11 2025 showing 2026-27 amounts (consistent with a Dec 2025 announcement). Separately, 'final' (as opposed to preliminary) CHT amounts for a fiscal year are determined about 6 months after that fiscal year ends (e.g., final 2025-26 amounts determined September 2026), per the same page's note, but this appears to be a data-finalization step rather than a public announcement event.

targetReport.title: Equalization Program
targetReport.description: The federal unconditional transfer that brings provinces with below-average fiscal capacity up to a per capita standard, calculated under Part I of the Federal-Provincial Fiscal Arrangements Act. targetReport.title: Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009 on the application of the Protocol on the excessive deficit procedure
targetReport.description: The EDP Regulation — the instrument that turns the Treaty's excessive deficit procedure into a statistical reporting regime, and the second EU Regulation in this corpus to be modelled as a node after esa-2010. It matters here for Article 9, which compels into existence a published national document class that no other instrument this branch has followed produces: 'Member States shall provide the Commission (Eurostat) with a detailed inventory of the methods, procedures and sources used to compile actual deficit and debt data and the underlying government accounts' (Art. 9(1)), 'The inventories shall be updated following revisions in the methods, procedures and sources adopted by Member States' (Art. 9(3)), and 'Member States shall make their inventories public' (Art. 9(4)). Eurostat's own EDP inventories page states the consequence — 'Pursuant to Article 9 of Council regulation 479/2009 (as amended), all EU Member States are required to prepare and publish an EDP inventory' — and carries a live Inventory link for each of the 27. EUR-Lex titles it a '(Codified version)', codifying Council Regulation (EEC) No 3605/93. targetReport.title: Lei nº 14.663, de 28 de agosto de 2023 (política de valorização permanente do salário mínimo)
targetReport.description: The statute establishing Brazil's permanent minimum-wage valorisation policy, and the cleanest live INPC dependency located in this corpus. Art. 1º, quoted directly: "Esta Lei define o valor do salário mínimo a partir de 1º de maio de 2023, estabelece a política de valorização permanente do salário mínimo a vigorar a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2024, e altera os valores da tabela mensal do Imposto sobre a Renda da Pessoa Física (IRPF)..." Art. 3º caput sets the two-term formula: "Ficam estabelecidas as diretrizes para a política de valorização do salário mínimo a vigorar a partir de 2024, inclusive, a serem aplicadas em 1º de janeiro do respectivo ano, considerado que o valor decorrerá da soma do índice de medida da inflação do ano anterior, para a preservação do poder aquisitivo, com o índice correspondente ao crescimento real do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) de 2 (dois) anos anteriores, para fins de aumento real, conforme apuração nos termos deste artigo." § 1º names the index and its producer: "Os reajustes para a preservação do poder aquisitivo do salário mínimo corresponderão à variação do Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor (INPC), calculado e divulgado pela Fundação Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), acumulada nos 12 (doze) meses encerrados em novembro do exercício anterior ao do reajuste." § 4º names IBGE for the GDP term as well — "a taxa de crescimento real do PIB do segundo ano anterior ao da fixação do valor do salário mínimo, apurada pelo IBGE até o último dia útil do ano e divulgada no ano anterior ao de aplicação do aumento real" — but names no titled release, which is why no GDP edge is minted from this node (see _dropped). The statute also fixes what happens when the index is late, §§ 2º–3º: "Na hipótese de não divulgação do INPC referente a um ou mais meses compreendidos no período do cálculo até o último dia útil imediatamente anterior à vigência do reajuste, o Poder Executivo federal estimará os índices dos meses não disponíveis" and "os índices estimados permanecerão válidos para os fins do disposto nesta Lei, sem qualquer revisão, e os eventuais resíduos serão compensados no reajuste subsequente, sem retroatividade" — a documented fallback rule for a missing input, which is the kind of method fidelity this corpus exists to capture. One-off foundational instrument per Research.1.md §4, so no releases_per_year. Fetched at TIER A from planalto.gov.br (HTTP 200, 36,354 bytes) with a browser User-Agent header.
targetReport.cadence_note: A statute defining a method, applied each 1 January by a separate annual decree (br-decreto-salario-minimo). Art. 3º fixes the application date verbatim — "a serem aplicadas em 1º de janeiro do respectivo ano" — but the statute itself is not reissued.

results.basis: VERIFIED, TIER A SOURCE BUT NOT FROM THE DEPENDENT DOCUMENT'S OWN TEXT — the weakness is stated here rather than in a footnote. STN's FINBRA/SICONFI Cartilha states the obligation directly and by name: "O RREO deve ser elaborado seguindo as regras contidas no Manual de Demonstrativos Fiscais – MDF." The MDF's own scope sentence names the RREO again from the other side: "O MDF estabelece regras de harmonização a serem observadas, de forma permanente, pela Administração Pública para a elaboração do ... Relatório Resumido da Execução Orçamentária (RREO) ... e define orientações metodológicas, consoante os parâmetros definidos pela LRF." So the relationship is asserted twice in the same first-party document, in both directions. `methodology_depends_on` is the right type — the MDF is exactly a method manual, and "o RREO deve ser elaborado seguindo as regras contidas no MDF" is a compliance obligation, not a reference. What it is NOT is a statement from an actual RREO instance about its own inputs, and the project's rule asks for the dependent document's own text. A purist should re-source this edge from a filed RREO or from the MDF itself; it is minted at MEDIUM confidence rather than dropped because the source is the Secretaria that publishes all three documents. This edge sits alongside, and does not replace, br-rreo -> br-lc-101-2000 in br-fiscal-responsibility-law.json: statute supplies the required content, manual supplies the harmonised form.

targetReport.title: Manual de Demonstrativos Fiscais (MDF)
targetReport.publisher: Secretaria do Tesouro Nacional (STN), Ministério da Fazenda
targetReport.description: STN's standing methodological manual for the LRF's fiscal demonstratives — the direct sibling of br-mcasp (Manual de Contabilidade Aplicada ao Setor Público, br-fpm-population.json), covering the fiscal reports where MCASP covers the accounting standards. Its scope is defined verbatim in STN's own FINBRA Cartilha: "O RREO deve ser elaborado seguindo as regras contidas no Manual de Demonstrativos Fiscais – MDF. O MDF estabelece regras de harmonização a serem observadas, de forma permanente, pela Administração Pública para a elaboração do Anexo de Riscos Fiscais (ARF), do Anexo de Metas Fiscais (AMF), do Relatório Resumido da Execução Orçamentária (RREO) e do Relatório de Gestão Fiscal (RGF), e define orientações metodológicas, consoante os parâmetros definidos pela LRF." That single sentence names all four instruments it governs, two of which are already nodes (br-rreo, br-rgf), and states its own subordination to the LRF (br-lc-101-2000). Its reissue rule, also verbatim: "O MDF é constantemente atualizado, e a observância da edição vigente deve ser dada seguindo o exercício financeiro..." HONEST LIMITATION ON THIS NODE, stated rather than glossed: the MDF's own document and its own STN landing page were NOT fetched this round. Every quotation above is STN's description of the MDF inside the FINBRA/SICONFI Cartilha (TIER A, plain curl, genuine text PDF) — an authoritative first-party source for what the MDF is and what it governs, written by the same Secretaria that publishes it, but not the manual's own text. The `url` below therefore points at that Cartilha rather than at an unverified MDF URL. A future round should re-source this node from a specific numbered edition of the MDF itself, which would also give the node a real edition history in the shape br-mcasp already has.

release_schedule.note: Lei nº 8.443/1992 is the Organic Law of the Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) — a one-off foundational statute enacted by Congresso Nacional on 1992-07-16, published in the Diário Oficial da União and consolidated on Planalto's site (ccivil_03/leis/l8443.htm). It is not a recurring publication: there is no release calendar, no publisher-stated periodic rule, and no consistent annual/periodic pattern of new editions. Like other organic laws/codes, it is amended irregularly by subsequent legislation (leis ordinárias, leis complementares) whenever Congress acts, with no fixed cadence. releases_per_year=0.1 on file (implying roughly one 'release' per decade) is a rough proxy for irregular amendment frequency but should not be read as a real periodicity; recommend flagging this field as not meaningfully applicable to a foundational statute.

targetReport.title: Local Government Act, 2012 (Act No. 18 of 2012, Cap 40:01)
targetReport.description: Botswana's organic law establishing Councils' revenue base and the Auditor-General's mandate to audit them. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. Section 64 (Part X, 'Revenues of Councils, Accounts and Audits') states: 'The revenues of a Council shall consist of - ... (h) the grants as the Government may make to the Council'. Section 68(3) states: '[t]he accounts under subsection (2)... shall be audited by the Auditor General' -- the exact provision the Auditor-General's own reports cite as their mandate to name and audit all Town/City and District Councils (see bw-auditor-general-report-2018-2019 and bw-auditor-general-report-2019-2020). A separate provision (Part V, Rating) states: 'It shall be lawful for the Minister in his or her discretion to make a grant to the revenue of the Council in lieu of an owner's rate, on property vested in Government... not exceeding the amount which would have been payable except for the provisions of subsection 4 (a) and (c)' -- the exact statutory mechanism behind the Auditor-General's finding of a P23,246,480 unpaid grant-in-lieu-of-rates to Gaborone City Council. Hosted on botswanalaws.com, a private Botswana legal-database mirror, not gov.bw directly; treated as adequate per this branch's established sourcing precedent for verbatim government Act text. Supersedes the pre-2012 Local Government (District Councils) Act, Cap 40:01, whose section 44 carried the same revenue-list wording ('such grants as the Government may make to the council') under older section numbering -- the predecessor was not independently minted as a corpus node since current Auditor-General reports cite the 2012 Act's section numbering, not the older instrument's.

The Full Story

 The Statistical Institute of Jamaica (STATIN) is reporting that the Jamaican System of National Accounts has been updated to reflect international best practices, enhancing comparability and analytic relevance. The revisions to the Jamaican System of National Accounts include aligning the national accounts with the United Nations System of National Accounts 2008 (SNA 2008), adoption of the 2016 revision of the Jamaica Industrial Classification (JIC 2016), rebasing constant (real) price estimates from 2007 to 2015; and incorporating new and revised data into the gross domestic product (GDP) estimates. Acting Director of the Economic Accounting Division, STATIN, Walata Wallace, provided details on the changes during a virtual Economic Statistics Media Stakeholders Meeting on the revision to the Jamaica System of National Accounts, on July 3.

targetReport.title: Mortgage Qualifying Rate (Benchmark Rate for Insured Mortgages)
targetReport.description: Since April 6, 2020 the Bank of Canada has published a weekly benchmark rate used to determine the minimum qualifying rate for government-backed insured mortgages. It is calculated as the weekly median 5-year fixed insured mortgage rate drawn from federally backed mortgage insurance applications adjudicated by mortgage insurers, plus a buffer set by the Minister of Finance (initially 200 basis points). It is published on a Wednesday and takes effect the following Monday, replacing the older Bank of Canada 5-Year Benchmark Posted Mortgage Rate for this purpose.

release_schedule.rule: The new benchmark rate for insured mortgages (based on the weekly median 5-year fixed insured mortgage rate from federally-backed mortgage insurance applications, plus a 200 bps buffer) is published by the Bank of Canada every Wednesday, effective the following Monday.
release_schedule.note: Confirmed by Department of Finance's Feb 2020 announcement establishing the new benchmark rate methodology and weekly Wednesday publication schedule (effective April 6, 2020, replacing the prior 5-Year Benchmark Posted Rate). Corroborated by Bank of Canada's related posted-interest-rates page, which is also 'Typically published on Wednesdays by 14:30 ET' with the most recent data as of research date (2026-08-11) being from Wednesday 2026-08-05, consistent with a next release on Wednesday 2026-08-12. Could not directly confirm on bankofcanada.ca which exact page hosts the insured-mortgage benchmark rate series itself (searches only surfaced the Department of Finance policy announcement and BoC's general posted-rates page), so no url_correction is made without direct citation.

results.basis: CMHC does not set its own qualification rules for insured mortgages; the Minister of Finance does. OSFI's May 2021 MQR letter states plainly: "The Minister of Finance sets the qualification rules for insured mortgages." The Department of Finance backgrounder describes the same framework: "Mortgage insurance standards include requirements for a minimum down payment, and maximum mortgage amortization period, along with other factors such as minimum credit scores and maximum debt servicing levels. The standards also include minimum qualifying rates for insured mortgages", and notes the review was conducted by Finance "in consultation with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions, the Bank of Canada, and the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation."

targetReport.title: Minimum Qualifying Rate for Insured Mortgages (Government-Backed Mortgage Insurance Guarantee Framework)
targetReport.description: The Minister of Finance, not OSFI, sets the qualification rules for insured mortgages under Canada's government-backed mortgage insurance guarantee framework. Since April 6, 2020 the minimum qualifying rate for an insured mortgage has been the greater of the borrower's contract rate or the Bank of Canada's published Benchmark Rate. The Minister retains authority to adjust the buffer built into that benchmark.
targetReport.cadence_note: Changed by ministerial decision rather than on a schedule; major changes in 2016, 2020.

release_schedule.note: This is a policy framework/rule, not a periodic statistical report. The Feb 2020 announcement set the minimum qualifying rate formula (weekly median 5-year fixed insured mortgage rate + a 200bp buffer set by the Minister of Finance, with authority to adjust the buffer as needed). While the underlying benchmark RATE VALUE is republished weekly (Wednesdays, effective the following Monday) by the Bank of Canada, the FRAMEWORK/RULE itself (what this Dept of Finance report/announcement documents) has only been amended irregularly and unpredictably since 2020: e.g. Dec 2022 and Dec 2023 ministerial statements on the housing market, the Sept 2024 'Boldest Mortgage Reforms in Decades' announcement, the Dec 2024 in-force announcement, and a March 2025 Canada Gazette regulatory amendment (Insurable Housing Loan Regulations / Eligible Mortgage Loan Regulations). There is no stated cadence or fixed review interval for buffer/framework changes -- the Minister simply 'will have the authority to adjust the buffer' at will. This looks like a foundational policy instrument amended irregularly rather than a true recurring publication.

results.basis: Destatis states ESA 2010 as the legal basis of the German national accounts in the structured metadata of its own quality report: 'Scope of the statistics: national accounts of the Federation (EVAS No 81) … Legal bases: Regulation (EC) No 549/2013, European System of National and Regional Accounts (ESA) 2010, and supplementary and amending regulations … Periodicity: quarterly, annual'. The same report sets out the mechanism: 'The ESA 2010 is a European Regulation, which is binding for all EU member states as of 1 September 2014 (Council Regulation (EU) No. 549/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 21 May 2013, published in the Official Journal on 26 June 2013). It was implemented in Germany as part of the 2014 general revision. This regulation was amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/734 …'. Two further documents say the same in their own words: the GNI inventory ('in compliance with the European System of National Accounts (ESA) 2010' and 'based on the European System of Accounts (ESA) 2010') and the QNA inventory ('in compliance with the European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)'). relationship_type is methodology_depends_on rather than uses_data_from: ESA 2010 supplies no figures, it supplies the 'common standards, definitions, classifications and accounting rules that shall be used for compiling accounts and tables' (Regulation 549/2013, Article 1(2)(a)).

targetReport.title: European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)
targetReport.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
targetReport.description: The EU's national accounts framework, enacted as Regulation (EU) No 549/2013. Article 1(2) sets out its two parts: 'a methodology (Annex A) on common standards, definitions, classifications and accounting rules that shall be used for compiling accounts and tables on comparable bases for the purposes of the Union' and 'a programme (Annex B) setting out the time limits by which Member States shall transmit to the Commission (Eurostat) the accounts and tables'. Unlike the international standards already in this corpus, ESA 2010 is a Regulation — member states do not adopt it by choice — which is why the EU branch was expected to produce supranational-to-national edges the Canada/US pair lacks. Annex B turned out to name tables and deadlines rather than publications; see the _dropped entries here and in eu-draft-budget.json.
targetReport.cadence_note: A generational standard, revised roughly once every fifteen to twenty years: ESA 1995 preceded it, and a further revision is already anticipated. releases_per_year matches sna-2008 (0.05) so the two read at the same pulse rate; see _open_questions.

release_schedule.note: 2030 is Eurostat's stated aim, not a locked legal date — the ESA 2030 proposal is still in consultation.

targetReport.title: Loi n°122/AN/05/5ème L du 1er novembre 2005 portant statut de la Ville de Djibouti
targetReport.description: Djibouti-Ville's own organic statute law, fetched directly from the Ministère Délégué Chargé de la Décentralisation's own .gouv.dj domain. Article 2, verbatim (defining the city's three communes): "La ville de Djibouti comprend trois communes : - la commune dénommée «Ras-Dika» dont le territoire correspond à celui du 6ème Arrondissement, - la commune appelée «Boulaos» recouvre l'ensemble des territoires de premier, deuxième et troisième arrondissement, - et la commune dite «Balbala» sous le nom duquel se regroupent les territoires du 4ème et du 5ème arrondissement." Article 99, verbatim (on the Conseil de Djibouti's budget composition): "Le budget du Conseil de Djibouti est composé : - des donations et transferts de l'État ; - des ressources fiscales locales ; - des produits de l'exploitation des services et domaines ; - des taxes rémunératrices sur les services rendus ; - des participations des autres collectivités ; - des produits financiers ; - des produits de dons, legs et subventions ; - des produits de l'aliénation des biens de la collectivité." This is a direct structural analogue to the régions' Article 80 in Loi n°174/AN/02 (dj-loi-174-2002-decentralisation) — the same enumeration pattern/order, evidencing a consistent national budget-composition template across both régional and Djibouti-Ville tiers. Also confirmed on the same page: the budget must be voted "avant le 1er janvier" of the fiscal year, accounts reported by July 1, and deficits exceeding 5% of operating revenue trigger court intervention; Article 52 gives the Council authority to set local taxes within legal limits.
targetReport.cadence_note: One-off foundational instrument (organic municipal statute).

targetReport.title: Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council on European statistics
targetReport.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
targetReport.description: The framework Regulation for European statistics, and the legal spine EU/slices/README.md names alongside ESA 2010 and the EBS Regulation. Two of its articles do work across this corpus. Article 11 constitutes the European Statistics Code of Practice: 'The Code of Practice shall aim at ensuring public trust in European statistics by establishing how European statistics are to be developed, produced and disseminated in conformity with the statistical principles as set out in Article 2(1) and best international statistical practice', and 'The Code of Practice shall be reviewed and updated as necessary by the ESS Committee. The Commission shall publish amendments thereto.' Article 12(1) sets the seven quality criteria — relevance, accuracy, timeliness, punctuality, accessibility and clarity, comparability, coherence — that ESA 2010 Article 4(1) applies to transmitted data and that Implementing Regulation 2016/2304 structures the national quality reports around. Minted 2026-08-07 after G.50.md filed it deferred when EUR-Lex served nothing; the retry G.50 recommended succeeded.

release_schedule.note: Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 is a standing legal act (the framework regulation governing the European Statistical System), not a periodically released publication. It has been amended irregularly as legislative need arose — e.g. by Regulation (EU) 2015/759, Regulation (EU) 2019/2152 (ESS governance regulation), and most recently Regulation (EU) 2024/... (in force from 26 Dec 2024, reflected in the consolidated text CELEX:02009R0223-20241226). No article of the regulation sets a fixed periodic review/evaluation date, and no publisher calendar exists for future amendments — the timing of the next amendment (if any) depends on future Commission legislative proposals and cannot be computed.

The adjacent sentence in the same paragraph - 'The concepts defined in the SIMS standard are compatible with the common terminology established by the SDMX standard' - is Research.1.md section 5a language and carries nothing; the operative clause is 'are derived from'.
results.evidenceQuote: The 19 high-level concepts are derived from the statistical data and metadata exchange (SDMX) cross-domain concepts published in the SDMX glossary .

targetReport.title: SDMX Glossary
targetReport.description: The terminology component of the SDMX Content-Oriented Guidelines, and the published home of the SDMX cross-domain concepts that the ESS's own metadata structure is derived from. The COG's own introduction: 'The SDMX Glossary is an SDMX guideline containing concepts and related definitions that are useful for building and understanding data and metadata exchange arrangements based on SDMX. [...] The Glossary is closely linked to the cross-domain concepts as it also contains all these concepts, stating their definitions and context descriptions.' Maintained by the SDMX Statistical Working Group: 'The development and maintenance of the content-oriented guidelines is under the responsibility of the SDMX Statistical Working Group (SWG), which is made of 20 members from national and international organisations from the statistical and central banking worlds.' The seven SDMX sponsoring institutions are referred to as a group in that document but are nowhere enumerated in the text read, so the publisher field does not enumerate them either.
targetReport.cadence_note: The weakest cadence in this slice, and stated as such. The Glossary says of itself only that it is updated, with no interval: 'this list will grow and be updated as the SDMX guidelines are used in more and more statistical domains. The Glossary should thus be considered as a "living" document'. sdmx.org names 'The SDMx Glossary Version 2.1 (published in December 2020)'; the same page carries a 'January 2009 version' of the subject-matter domain classification and a February 2016 COG introduction. Roughly one version per decade on the versions observed; 0.1 is that count, not a commitment.

release_schedule.note: The SDMX Glossary is a reference document maintained by the SDMX Statistical Working Group (SWG), not a periodic statistical release. The current version 2.1 was published December 2020, revising prior editions with new/clarified concept definitions. The publisher's page (sdmx.org) states the glossary is subject to ongoing review by the SWG but gives no fixed update schedule, calendar, or stated periodicity rule. Given the multi-year gaps between editions and absence of any announced cadence, this fits 'irregular' rather than a computable schedule.

targetReport.title: Consumer Price Index (Ethiopian Statistics Services)
targetReport.description: Ethiopia's official monthly CPI, produced by ESS (formerly the Central Statistical Agency/CSA). VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via ESS's own site: 'Published monthly', described as 'the principal measure of inflation'; ESS's own framing states its statistics 'support evidence-based policy decisions, wage and income adjustments, business planning, and economic research'. Confirmed via Grok's round: Ethiopia is on the IMF's e-GDDS dissemination tier (not full SDDS), per the IMF's own 2019 press release announcing Ethiopia's e-GDDS implementation -- the same weaker tier already found for Kenya, now a second country on this node. release_schedule.rule: Starting from May 2026, national accounts (annual, quarterly, and quarterly sector accounts combined into one set of statistics) are released eight times a year: quarterly national accounts data are released within two months after the end of the quarter (i.e. in February, May, August and November), and quarterly sector accounts data follow approximately two weeks later (March, June, September and December). Final annual figures are completed in December once supply and use tables are finalised.

targetReport.title: Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009 on the application of the Protocol on the excessive deficit procedure
targetReport.description: The EDP Regulation — the instrument that turns the Treaty's excessive deficit procedure into a statistical reporting regime, and the second EU Regulation in this corpus to be modelled as a node after esa-2010. It matters here for Article 9, which compels into existence a published national document class that no other instrument this branch has followed produces: 'Member States shall provide the Commission (Eurostat) with a detailed inventory of the methods, procedures and sources used to compile actual deficit and debt data and the underlying government accounts' (Art. 9(1)), 'The inventories shall be updated following revisions in the methods, procedures and sources adopted by Member States' (Art. 9(3)), and 'Member States shall make their inventories public' (Art. 9(4)). Eurostat's own EDP inventories page states the consequence — 'Pursuant to Article 9 of Council regulation 479/2009 (as amended), all EU Member States are required to prepare and publish an EDP inventory' — and carries a live Inventory link for each of the 27. EUR-Lex titles it a '(Codified version)', codifying Council Regulation (EEC) No 3605/93. Note that the Regulation names no member state's inventory by title: AGENCY ONLY at exactly the point where a title would have produced a downward edge.
targetReport.cadence_note: Derived from an observed amendment record, not from a stated rate — see _open_questions. Adopted 25 May 2009; EUR-Lex lists exactly two consolidated versions, 19/08/2010 and 01/09/2014, with 01/09/2014 flagged as the current version. Two amendments across the 17 years to 2026.

targetReport.title: European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)
targetReport.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
targetReport.description: The EU's national accounts framework, enacted as Regulation (EU) No 549/2013. Article 1(2) sets out its two parts: 'a methodology (Annex A) on common standards, definitions, classifications and accounting rules that shall be used for compiling accounts and tables on comparable bases for the purposes of the Union' and 'a programme (Annex B) setting out the time limits by which Member States shall transmit to the Commission (Eurostat) the accounts and tables'. Unlike the international standards already in this corpus, ESA 2010 is a Regulation — member states do not adopt it by choice — which is why the EU branch was expected to produce supranational-to-national edges the Canada/US pair lacks. Annex B turned out to name tables and deadlines rather than publications; see the _dropped entries here and in eu-draft-budget.json.
targetReport.cadence_note: A generational standard, revised roughly once every fifteen to twenty years: ESA 1995 preceded it, and a further revision is already anticipated. releases_per_year matches sna-2008 (0.05) so the two read at the same pulse rate; see _open_questions.

results.window:
El concepto de
endeudamiento que proporciona esta publicación es el más amplio posible, porque comprende la totalidad de los pasivos
contraídos por las AAPP, independientemente de su naturaleza (emisión de moneda, valores representativos de deuda,
participaciones en el capital y en fondos de inversión, préstamos no comerciales, a corto y a largo plazo, en euros y en monedas
distintas del euro, créditos comerciales y otras obligaciones pendientes de pago). En cuanto a la valoración de los pasivos
incluidos en este concepto, se sigue la metodología que establece el Sistema Europeo de Cuentas Económicas Integradas de
2010 (SEC 2010) descrita en la nota metodológica de las CFEE que se difunde en la página web del Banco de España
(http://www.bde.es/webbde/SES/Secciones/Publicaciones/PublicacionesSeriadas/NotasEstadisticas/07/Fic/nest05.pdf) y que
se caracteriza por utilizar los valores de mercado en la valoración de los saldos y flujos de los pasivos materializados en valores
representativos de deuda. La variación de este endeudamiento se explica por: a) La necesidad neta de financiación, es decir, los gastos no financieros
menos los ingresos no financieros, según el criterio de la Contabilidad Nacional, que, a su vez, debe seguir las normas del SEC
2010; b) El incremento neto de activos financieros y, c) Los ajustes por cambios de valoración (que se producen, por ejemplo, en
el caso de los valores representativos de deuda y los pasivos en monedas distintas del euro).

targetReport.title: Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009 on the application of the Protocol on the excessive deficit procedure
targetReport.description: The EDP Regulation — the instrument that turns the Treaty's excessive deficit procedure into a statistical reporting regime, and the second EU Regulation in this corpus to be modelled as a node after esa-2010. It matters here for Article 9, which compels into existence a published national document class that no other instrument this branch has followed produces: 'Member States shall provide the Commission (Eurostat) with a detailed inventory of the methods, procedures and sources used to compile actual deficit and debt data and the underlying government accounts' (Art. 9(1)), 'The inventories shall be updated following revisions in the methods, procedures and sources adopted by Member States' (Art. 9(3)), and 'Member States shall make their inventories public' (Art. 9(4)). Eurostat's own EDP inventories page states the consequence — 'Pursuant to Article 9 of Council regulation 479/2009 (as amended), all EU Member States are required to prepare and publish an EDP inventory' — and carries a live Inventory link for each of the 27. EUR-Lex titles it a '(Codified version)', codifying Council Regulation (EEC) No 3605/93. Note that the Regulation names no member state's inventory by title: AGENCY ONLY at exactly the point where a title would have produced a downward edge.

targetReport.title: European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)
targetReport.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
targetReport.description: The EU's national accounts framework, enacted as Regulation (EU) No 549/2013. Article 1(2) sets out its two parts: 'a methodology (Annex A) on common standards, definitions, classifications and accounting rules that shall be used for compiling accounts and tables on comparable bases for the purposes of the Union' and 'a programme (Annex B) setting out the time limits by which Member States shall transmit to the Commission (Eurostat) the accounts and tables'. Unlike the international standards already in this corpus, ESA 2010 is a Regulation — member states do not adopt it by choice — which is why the EU branch was expected to produce supranational-to-national edges the Canada/US pair lacks. Annex B turned out to name tables and deadlines rather than publications; see the _dropped entries here and in eu-draft-budget.json.

The weight calculation has as follows:
 
 
 The National Accounts expenditure for the year t-2 is taken at the 4-digit code level, after deducting the following expenditures: 
 
 Drugs,
 
 Imputed rents,
 
 Hot water, steam and ice,
 
 Gambling,
 
 Prostitution,
 
 FISIM,
 
 Life insurance,
 
 Public insurance connected with health
 
 
 
 The expenditure of 3-digit codes is allocated proportionally to the 4 and 5-digit level, using the data of the National Accounts and the Household Budget Survey (HBS) respectively, both for the year t-2.

results.window: Euro area inflation is measured by the MUICP (‘Monetary Union Index of Consumer Prices’ as defined in Council Regulation (EC) No 2494/95 of 23 October 1995) which is the official euro area aggregate. Country weights are computed every year reflecting the country’s share of the household final monetary consumption expenditure in the euro area total.

At ECOICOP ver.2 5-digit level, weights used in the current year t are based on national accounts data referring to t-2, estimated in line with the domestic concept, that are further adjusted using additional sources in order to make them representative for t-1. results.basis:
VERIFIED DIRECTLY BY THIS SESSION (2026-08-09) -- Eurostat's 'Farm structure (ef)' metadata page re-fetched first-hand, and the sentence now pinned to its section: it sits in section 3.4, Statistical concepts and definitions. "Both the censuses and the sample surveys are aimed at producing a variety of information on specific CAP targets, as well as providing a basis for extrapolating Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN) data." Direction is FSDN -> FSS, as the original lead reasoned: a ~75 000-farm sample capped by Regulation (EC) No 1217/2009 Article 5(3) at "105 000 for the Community" needs a population framework to extrapolate to the 3.5 million farms it claims to represent, and this record says the FSS supplies it. Typed `methodology_depends_on` rather than `uses_data_from`: what passes is a weighting/extrapolation framework, not FSS observations feeding into FSDN records. TWO CAVEATS, both stated rather than smoothed over. First, the evidence is ONE-SIDED: it is Eurostat asserting what its survey is used for, and DG AGRI's own FSDN page -- read in full this session -- names neither the Farm Structure Survey, nor integrated farm statistics, nor Regulation (EU) 2018/1091, nor Eurostat anywhere. The producer of the dependent product has not been found stating the dependency. Second, the quoted sentence still says FADN, the network's pre-2023 name; the node is minted under its current name, FSDN, so the edge crosses a rename. Nothing found this session suggests the extrapolation arrangement itself changed with the rename, but nothing found confirms it either -- a successor should look for the same statement in FSDN-era methodology (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2746 is the obvious place, since DG AGRI's page says it carries the farm-selection methodology).

CORROBORATED FROM THE RECEIVING SIDE, 2026-08-09 (closing G.64.md cheap check 3 / this file's own _open_questions item 4). The first caveat above -- that only Eurostat, the supplying side, had been found stating this dependency -- no longer holds. FSDN's own implementing regulation, Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2746 of 25 October 2024 ('laying down rules for the application of Council Regulation (EC) No 1217/2009 setting up the Farm Sustainability Data Network...'), fetched directly from EUR-Lex (CELEX:32024R2746), states in Annex III ('Models and methods for selection plan preparation'): 'all relevant types and sizes of farming represented in the integrated farm statistics (IFS) census or survey are to be covered at the level of detail which provides representative results on important farm groups, within the limits of the sample size.' 'Integrated farm statistics' is the Farm Structure Survey's own legal name -- Regulation (EU) 2018/1091, which this node's own description cites as its re-founding instrument, is titled 'on integrated farm statistics'. Recital (5) of 2024/2746 cross-references the same instrument directly: 'These standard outputs need to be established by product and should align with the list of core structural data variables set out in Annex III to Regulation (EU) 2018/1091 of the European Parliament and of the Council.' So the FSDN sample-selection methodology names the FSS/IFS census as the population it must represent, on its own side of the relationship, independent of Eurostat's own metadata page. The second caveat (the edge crosses FADN's rename to FSDN) is unaffected -- 2024/2746 is itself an FSDN-era instrument and does not use the name FADN, so it does not help there either way.

targetReport.title: Farm Structure Survey (FSS)
targetReport.description: Eurostat's recurring survey of the structure of agricultural holdings across the EU, run in one form or another since 1966. Eurostat's own metadata page states: 'The data describe the structure of agricultural holdings providing the general characteristics of farms and farmers and information on their land, livestock and labour force. They also describe production methods, rural development measures and agro-environmental aspects... The aggregated results are disseminated through statistical tables.' Legally re-founded by Regulation (EU) 2018/1091 ('on integrated farm statistics'), which fixed the current data collections at reference years 2020, 2023 and 2026 -- a census in 2020, sample surveys in 2023 and 2026 -- each covering at least 98% of the EU's utilised agricultural area and livestock units. Eurostat's own metadata states the FSS 'provid[es] a basis for extrapolating Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN) data' -- see _dropped.
targetReport.cadence_note: Currently fixed at reference years 2020, 2023, 2026 by Regulation (EU) 2018/1091 Article 5 -- a 3-year interval, with results 'disseminated 2 years after the reference year' (Eurostat metadata page, 'Frequency of dissemination'). Historically (1989/1990 through 2016) reference years averaged roughly one every 2.6 years on a 10-year agricultural-census cycle with 2-3 intermediate sample surveys between censuses. See _open_questions.

release_schedule.rule: Regulation (EU) 2018/1091, Article 5: 'Member States shall collect and provide the core structural data ... for the reference years 2020, 2023 and 2026.' Article 12 sets Member State transmission deadlines of 12 months after the end of the 2023/2026 reference years (15 months for 2020). Eurostat's own metadata for this dataset (ef_sims.htm, Accuracy/Timeliness section) states: 'Results are disseminated 2 years after the reference year.'
release_schedule.note: FSS is run on a 3-year cycle mandated by Regulation (EU) 2018/1091 (reference years 2020 [census], 2023, 2026); the regulation as currently in force does not specify years beyond 2026. As of the current date (2026-08-11) the 2026 reference-year survey is the cycle underway; per Eurostat's own metadata, results for a given reference year are disseminated about 2 years later, so 2026-reference-year results are expected around 2028 (exact month not published). This matches the releases_per_year=0.33 (~once every 3 years) already on file.

targetReport.title: Consumer Price Index (Ghana Statistical Service)
targetReport.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via GSS's own CPI Technical Methodology Manual (v5, published October 2020) and its own recent press releases. The v5 manual: 'GSS uses 13 out of the 15 Divisions as distinguished by the COICOP manual', organised into '44 Groups, 98 Classes, 156 Subclasses, and 307 Item-level observations', and 'to order products into these different categories, GSS uses the United Nations Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 2018 manual.' Elementary aggregates: 'GSS uses the unweighted Jevons Index... the geometric mean of price relatives.' The v5 manual describes the then-current series on 'the whole year of 2018 as the price reference period' with 'weights based on the Ghana Living Standard Surveys 7 (GLSS7) from 2016/2017', and credits input from 'Statistics Denmark, and the International Monetary Fund (IMF)' plus ILO CPI-manual guidance. GSS has since rebased: the September 2025 press release (published 1 October 2025) states 'the price reference period has been updated to 2021 (2021=100)' with the weight reference period still 2017 -- confirmed independently, distinct from and more current than the v5 manual's own 2018=100 description. The rebase's own dedicated methodology note (as opposed to a press-release mention) was not located this session.

GSS's own 2025 Statistical Product Release Calendar PDF confirms CPI is scheduled in Week 1 (or Week 2) of each month, but states the calendar 'will be updated quarterly' and no 2026 edition with exact dates was found online, so the September 2026 (for August 2026 data) date is inferred from the pattern rather than a published calendar entry.

targetReport.title: Local Governance Act, 2016 (Act 936)
targetReport.description: The national statute establishing District Assemblies (including AMA) and their property-rating powers: "A general rate may be (a) a rate payable by the owner of premises within the district on the rateable value of the premises... targetReport.publisher: República de Guinea Ecuatorial (official constitutional text, hosted by FAOLEX)
targetReport.description: Equatorial Guinea's constitution. Artículo 3, apartados 4-5: "4. Se divide para los fines administrativos y económicos en Regiones, Provincias, Distritos y Municipios. 5. La ley determina los límites y las denominaciones de las regiones, provincias, distritos y municipios." Título Cuarto, "De las Corporaciones Locales," Artículo 131: "Las Corporaciones Locales son instituciones con personalidad jurídica propia, encargadas del gobierno y administración de las regiones, provincias, distritos y municipios. Artículo 132.2: "La ley determina las competencias, el funcionamiento, la jurisdicción y la composición de las Corporaciones Locales." The Constitution itself establishes Municipios as one of four administrative/economic-division tiers and gives Corporaciones Locales legal personality, but explicitly delegates all finance/competency detail to ordinary law rather than stating a mechanism itself — the implementing law is Ley Número 1/2003 (see gq-ley-1-2003-administracion-local). Independently downloaded and text-extracted via pdftotext, not AI-summarized. Equatorial Guinea's official BOE portal (boe.gob.gq) could not be reached this round (503 Service Unavailable) to cross-verify against a more-authoritative host; the FAOLEX copy was used and is treated as reliable.

targetReport.title: European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)
targetReport.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
targetReport.description: The EU's national accounts framework, enacted as Regulation (EU) No 549/2013. Article 1(2) sets out its two parts: 'a methodology (Annex A) on common standards, definitions, classifications and accounting rules that shall be used for compiling accounts and tables on comparable bases for the purposes of the Union' and 'a programme (Annex B) setting out the time limits by which Member States shall transmit to the Commission (Eurostat) the accounts and tables'. Unlike the international standards already in this corpus, ESA 2010 is a Regulation — member states do not adopt it by choice — which is why the EU branch was expected to produce supranational-to-national edges the Canada/US pair lacks. Annex B turned out to name tables and deadlines rather than publications; see the _dropped entries here and in eu-draft-budget.json.

targetReport.title: Indice des prix à la consommation national (IPCN)
targetReport.publisher: Service central de la statistique et des études économiques (STATEC)
targetReport.description: Luxembourg's national-only consumer price index, published alongside the IPCH but scoped to resident consumption only. Règlement grand-ducal du 20 décembre 1999, Art. 1er: 'En complément à l'indice des prix à la consommation harmonisé (IPCH), le STATEC établit un indice des prix à la consommation national (IPCN), qui se conforme aux mêmes principes et concepts méthodologiques. Toutefois, la couverture géographique de l'IPCN se limite à la seule population résidante; elle exclut la consommation des non-résidants.' Named as the input to Luxembourg's own wage/salary indexation mechanism at Art. 4(1) of the same regulation: 'Pour les besoins de l'échelle mobile des salaires et traitements, l'indice national des prix à la consommation (IPCN)... est raccordé à la base 100 au 1er janvier 1948.'
targetReport.cadence_note: Same monthly cadence as lu-statec-ipch -- both established by the same Art. 1er, 'chaque mois'.

release_schedule.note: STATEC's official 'Calendrier de diffusion' (release calendar, last updated 2026-07-31) lists a monthly entry 'Indice des prix à la consommation (CPI)' with a specific day-of-month release date for each reference month; this entry covers the joint monthly IPCN/IPCH press release. Dates are explicitly labeled by STATEC as provisional ('dates prévisionnelles de diffusion et sont susceptibles d'être modifiées'). results.window: As for the other factors, they are related to changes in the quality and quantity of goods and services and the amounts spent on them. Therefore, the consumer price index is a measure of price changes only and not a measure of changes in the cost of living. The consumer price index also differs from the retail price index, in that the latter relates to the prices of all goods that are included in retail trade, while the interest in the consumer price index is focused on the goods and services purchased by the consumer, as it is limited only to measuring the change during a period of time.

targetReport.title: Survey of Household Spending (SHS)
targetReport.description: Annual national household survey collecting detailed information on what Canadian households spend on food, shelter, clothing, transportation and other categories. Its principal downstream use is to supply the expenditure detail used to construct Consumer Price Index basket weights, particularly at low levels of product and geographic aggregation. Results are released as Table 11-10-0222-01 and associated Daily articles.

release_schedule.note: StatCan's own survey metadata (IMDB, SDDS 3508) states the Survey of Household Spending is conducted 'Every 2 years' (reference years 2019, 2021, 2023, 2025, ...), so data collection follows a fixed 2-year cycle. However, there is no published release calendar and the actual publication lag after each reference year has been highly irregular: 2019 reference-year data was released 2021-01-22 (~13 months after year-end), 2021 data was released 2023-10-18 (~22 months after year-end), and 2023 data was released 2025-05-21 (~17 months after year-end) — see The Daily releases dq210122b, dq231018a, and dq250521a. Because both the exact release month and the lag length vary substantially cycle to cycle, no specific next release date can be reliably computed. 2025 reference-year data collection ran through roughly February 2026 per StatCan's respondent portal, so the next release (for 2025 data) is expected at some point in 2026-2027, but no concrete date or calendar entry has been published by StatCan as of 2026-08-11.

results.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, and the strongest breadth edge found for India this round -- the dependent document both NAMES the source and REPUBLISHES its numbers. The footnote to ANNEX-4's "Share (Per cent)" column reads: "* As per accepted recommendations of the Sixteenth Finance Commission, the States' share has been fixed at 41% of the net proceeds of shareable Central Taxes." The column it annotates reproduces FC16 Volume I Table 8.9 digit for digit: "Andhra Pradesh 4.217 | Arunachal Pradesh 1.354 | Assam 3.258 | Bihar 9.948 | Chhattisgarh 3.304 | Goa 0.365 | Gujarat 3.755 | Haryana 1.361 | Himachal Pradesh 0.914 | … | Uttar Pradesh 17.619 | Uttarakhand 1.141 | West Bengal 7.215" against FC16's own "Andhra Pradesh 4.217 / Arunachal Pradesh 1.354 / Assam 3.258 / Bihar 9.948 / Chhattisgarh 3.304 / Goa 0.365 / Gujarat 3.755 / Haryana 1.361 / Himachal Pradesh 0.914 / Jharkhand 3.357 / Karnataka 4.131 / Kerala 2.382 / Madhya Pradesh 7.347 / Maharashtra 6.441 …". `uses_data_from` rather than `cites`: the shares are literal computational inputs to the state-wise distribution the annex publishes, not a background reference. This is also the edge that makes the Indian chain load-bearing rather than merely documentary -- it connects a Commission recommendation to the money actually appropriated.

targetReport.title: Sixteenth Finance Commission, Report for 2026-31, Volume I — Main Report
targetReport.publisher: Sixteenth Finance Commission (constitutional body under Article 280), Government of India
targetReport.description: The most recent Finance Commission report, superseding the Fifteenth as the operative award. Vertical devolution, verbatim (Summary of Recommendations, para 7.68): "3. We recommend that the States' share in the divisible pool is retained at 41 per cent." — the same headline share as the outgoing Fifteenth Finance Commission (see `in-fc15-report`), a real continuity fact rather than a coincidence of rounding. Horizontal devolution formula, verbatim (Table 8.8): "Table 8.8 Formula for Horizontal Devolution — Criteria / Weight (percentage): Population (2011) 17.5; Demographic Performance 10; Area 10; Forest 10; Per Capita GSDP Distance 42.5; Contribution to GDP 10; Total 100." On its population criterion the report names its source directly: "8.15 We next provide an evaluation of the criteria..." / "we rely on the 2011 Census figures. In this respect, we have fully transitioned from the 1971 Census population to the 2011 Census population data." — i.e. the Population (2011) criterion is sourced to the Census of India 2011 (Registrar General & Census Commissioner), a different producer from MoSPI, which the report cites elsewhere (GDP/GSDP and household consumption survey data) but not for population. No separate node exists for the Census of India 2011 this round — no citable URL for the census itself was located in this research pass, only FC16's own textual reliance on it — so this paragraph is the record of that dependency until a Census node can be built with its own evidence (see `_dropped`). Searched directly for "Consumer Price Index", "CPI" and "MoSPI" across the full Volume I text: the report cites MoSPI repeatedly for GDP/GSDP and consumption-survey data but never for CPI or any inflation index — a genuine negative finding (see `_dropped`), not an oversight in this transcription.

We recommend retaining the vertical share of 41 per cent of the divisible pool of taxes for the States during the award period of this Commission." — the identical 41 per cent headline figure the Sixteenth Commission later retained. Horizontal devolution formula, verbatim (Table 6.4): "Table 6.4: Criteria and Weights assigned for Horizontal Devolution — Population 15.0; Area 15.0; Forest and ecology 10.0; Income distance 45.0; Tax and fiscal efforts 2.5; Demographic performance 12.5" (Total 100.0). results.basis: VERIFIED, BUT WITH A WEAKNESS STATED EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN SILENTLY UPGRADED -- read this basis before relying on the edge. BRICS/G.1 scoped `in-rbi-act-45za` deliberately narrowly, to only what Section 45ZA's own text establishes, because it could not verify the notified target behind an RBI bot-wall and a CAPTCHA-gated gazette search. This round did NOT retrieve the literal signed gazette instrument either (S.O. 2088(E) -- see `_dropped` for the full record of attempts). What it did retrieve is the same statement from TWO INDEPENDENT PRIMARY GOVERNMENT-OF-INDIA PUBLISHERS. Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Finance, 5 August 2016: "Under sub-section (1) of section 45ZA of the RBI Act, the Central Government, in consultation with the RBI, determines the inflation target in terms of the Consumer Price Index (CPI), once in every five years. This target would be notified in the Official Gazette." and "Determination and notification of Inflation Target — In exercise of the powers conferred by section 45ZA of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, the Central Government, in consultation with RBI, has fixed the inflation target … Inflation Target: Four per cent. Upper tolerance level: Six per cent. Lower tolerance level: Two per cent." And the Reserve Bank's own Monetary Policy Overview: "Under Section 45ZA, the Central Government, in consultation with the RBI, determines the inflation target in terms of the Consumer Price Index (CPI), once in five years and notifies it in the Official Gazette." THE MECHANISM IS ALSO CURRENT, which matters for tense: "In its second review, on March 25, 2026, the Central Government retained the inflation target and the tolerance band for the next 5-year period – April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2031." TWO EXPLICIT LIMITS ON THIS EDGE: (1) the citation comes from the Government's own explanatory statements ABOUT section 45ZA, not from the section's four corners nor from a retrieved gazette instrument; (2) the "(Combined)" qualifier is NOT evidenced anywhere reachable and is deliberately absent from this basis and from the node -- every primary text retrieved says "Consumer Price Index (CPI)" without it. `cites` rather than `uses_data_from` precisely because of limit (1): a stronger type would assert a computational relationship the retrieved documents do not themselves state.

results.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, and structurally the most important edge in this file: `in-fc15-report` sits inside India's main eleven-node component, so this single citation is what attaches the whole Finance Commission cluster -- Constitution, Commission reports, Explanatory Memoranda, Union Budget, RBI State Finances, CAG -- to the international layer. FC15 Volume I cites the WEO in two footnotes supporting its macroeconomic narrative: "1 World Economic Outlook, October 2020" and "4 World Economic Outlook October 2020, International Monetary Fund". `uses_data_from` rather than `methodology_depends_on`, deliberately: the WEO supplies comparator data and growth figures the Commission reasons from; it is not a standard the Commission's methodology conforms to. ON THE EDITION QUESTION, which the research flagged and which is worth settling here as a corpus rule: `imf-weo` is NOT edition-split and should not be, because the WEO is a RECURRING PUBLICATION, not a standard with successor editions held as separate nodes. This corpus models a recurring release as one node covering all its issues -- `br-ipca` covers every month, `cn-nbs-statistical-communique` every year -- so citing the October 2020 issue is like citing a particular month of a monthly index, and points at the series node correctly. That is a different situation from SNA 2008 versus SNA 2025, which are successive STANDARDS deliberately held apart. WEAKNESS STATED: this is a footnote citation, the weakest form of dependency in this project's taxonomy. A third mention (the source line of Figure 2.2, "Sources: IMF, World Economic Outlook, and staff calculations") is unversioned and would not qualify alone.

targetReport.title: Seventh Strategic Energy Plan (第7次エネルギー基本計画) — February 2025 Cabinet Decision
targetReport.publisher: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) / Agency for Natural Resources and Energy; Cabinet Decision
targetReport.description: Mid- to long-term energy policy framework adopted by Cabinet Decision in February 2025. Sets the indicative power-generation mix for FY2040, including approximately 20 % nuclear power (alongside 40–50 % renewables and 30–40 % thermal with decarbonisation measures). Explicitly takes the lessons of the Great East Japan Earthquake and Fukushima Daiichi accident as the starting point, prioritising safety (S+3E: Safety, Energy Security, Economic Efficiency, Environment).
targetReport._notes: Prime static + recurring-citation policy node for Japan’s nuclear trajectory. The ~20 % nuclear share by FY2040 is the official benchmark against which restart progress, capacity utilisation and investment decisions are measured. Continuously cited in energy-balance, CO₂ and industrial-policy analysis. Complements the disaster-management cluster by embedding the post-Fukushima safety-first principle into long-term energy strategy.

targetReport.title: Statistics Act (Act No. 53 of 2007) — 統計法
targetReport.publisher: National Diet of Japan / Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC)
targetReport.description: Foundational statute that comprehensively reformed Japan’s official statistics system. Defines official statistics as information infrastructure, establishes fundamental statistics (基幹統計) and fundamental statistical surveys, creates the Statistics Commission, requires a Master Plan concerning the Development of Official Statistics, and sets rules for statistical surveys, confidentiality, secondary use, and coordination across the highly decentralised Japanese statistical system. Replaced the 1947 Statistics Act.
targetReport._notes:
Prime static + recurring-citation node — direct analogue of Mexico’s LSNIEG and Argentina’s Ley 17.622.

Article 1 states the purpose: ‘to promote systematic and efficient development of official statistics and to ensure the usefulness thereof through specifying basic matters concerning the production and provision of official statistics, and thereby to contribute to sound development of the national economy and enhancement of the living standards of the citizens.’

Official statistics are explicitly recognised as ‘information infrastructure’ usable not only by administration but by society as a whole. Fundamental statistics include the Population Census statistics, National Accounts, and other statistics designated by the Minister of Internal Affairs and Communications. Every subsequent methodological document, survey approval, and quality report cites the 2007 Act as the legal foundation. No independent publication cadence is required; continuous institutional citation satisfies the expanded node definition.

 調査の目的

 
 　経済産業省生産動態統計調査は、統計法に基づく基幹統計『経済産業省生産動態統計』を作成するための基幹統計調査です。この調査は、鉱工業生産の動態を明らかにし、鉱工業に関する施策の基礎資料を得ることを目的としています。 調査の沿革


 【調査開始年】

 昭和23年（1948年）開始

 【調査の沿革】

 
 　生産動態統計調査は、連合国軍総司令部の要請を踏まえ、昭和23年1月（1948年1月）に生産動態の把握及び経済統制下における物資の需給調整上の資料としての利用を目的に開始され、昭和26年（1951年）の経済統制の解除により物資の需給調整という副次的利用目的が大幅に後退したのを契機として、昭和28年（1953年）に経済統計への移行に重点を置いた大幅な改正が行われました。その後は、昭和48年（1973年）のコンピュータ処理化に伴う統計の体系整備のための調査品目・調査項目の簡素化、昭和56年（1981年）の商鉱工業エネルギー消費統計調査（現在の経済産業省特定業種石油等消費統計調査）の開始に伴うエネルギー関連項目の簡素化がされました。

results.basis: Record 2612, Data sources: 'The statistics compiled by SEPH are based on a census of administrative records for all in-scope establishments with employees that can be found on the Business Register. Administrative information for total gross monthly payrolls and the total number of employees for the last pay period in the month are obtained from payroll deduction (PD7 form) accounts maintained by Canada Revenue Agency.' A census of these records rather than a sample of employers, which makes this the strongest available characterisation short of calculated_from. Held at uses_data_from because SEPH applies estimation on top — the same record describes model groups and a Business Payrolls Survey filling gaps — so the payroll figure is not arithmetic on the remittances alone.
results.evidenceQuote: Administrative information for total gross monthly payrolls and the total number of employees for the last pay period in the month are obtained from payroll deduction (PD7 form) accounts maintained by Canada Revenue Agency.

targetReport.title: CRA payroll deduction (PD7) accounts
targetReport.description: The administrative remittance records behind SEPH, and the first terminus in the graph. IMDB record 2612 names them as the primary input: 'Administrative information for total gross monthly payrolls and the total number of employees for the last pay period in the month are obtained from payroll deduction (PD7 form) accounts maintained by Canada Revenue Agency.' SEPH is a census of these records rather than a survey of employers, so the entire monthly payroll estimate — which four federal and provincial benefit formulas are calculated from — rests on a remittance form. There is no PD7 publication, no release schedule and no url: what exists is a form employers file and an agency that holds the results.
targetReport.cadence_note: A terminus has no publication cadence, so this number is the collection rhythm rather than a release rate: PD7 remittances are monthly, and record 2612 describes the payroll figure as covering 'the last pay period in the month'. Read it as how often the data behind this node changes, not as how often anything appears.

results.basis: Record 2101, Use of Administrative Data: 'In an attempt to alleviate response burden, especially for small businesses, the MSM derives sales data for low-revenue establishments from Goods and Service Tax (GST) files using a ratio estimator.' The word 'derives' plus a named estimator is a direct-input claim; it applies to a stated subset of establishments rather than the whole, which is why this is uses_data_from and not calculated_from.
results.evidenceQuote: In this methodology, a model that describes the relationship between estimated sales coming from the MSM and sales coming from the Goods and Services Tax (GST) data at a small level of geography is combined with traditional estimates obtained from the weighted MSM sample.

targetReport.title: Goods and Services Tax (GST) administrative files
targetReport.description: GST remittance records, used to avoid surveying small manufacturers. IMDB record 2101: 'Managing response burden is an ongoing challenge for Statistics Canada. In an attempt to alleviate response burden, especially for small businesses, the MSM derives sales data for low-revenue establishments from Goods and Service Tax (GST) files using a ratio estimator.' So part of the monthly manufacturing sales figure — which the monthly GDP programme uses as its indicator for most manufacturing industries — is not collected at all but estimated from tax remittances.
targetReport.cadence_note: A terminus has no publication cadence. GST filing frequency is set by the filer's revenue — monthly, quarterly or annually — and record 2101 does not state which vintage the MSM reads. 4 is the middle case and is a guess, flagged as such rather than left to look measured.

results.window: Estimates of sales for fifteen census metropolitan areas (CMA) have been derived by using a small area estimation (SAE) technique based on a Fay-Herriot methodology. In this methodology, a model that describes the relationship between estimated sales coming from the MSM and sales coming from the Goods and Services Tax (GST) data at a small level of geography is combined with traditional estimates obtained from the weighted MSM sample. The resulting small area estimates are often significantly more precise than standard MSM weighted estimates, particularly for areas where the latter become unreliable due to small area sample sizes.

targetReport.title: Local Government Act 2011 (Act No. 36 of 2011), Section 83 — Grants to Municipal City Council, Municipal Town Council or District Council
targetReport.publisher: Attorney-General's Office, Mauritius (Revised Laws of Mauritius)
targetReport.description: Mauritius's national local-government statute, as consolidated in the Revised Laws of Mauritius (page marked "L18 – 52"). Section 83, "Grants to Municipal City Council, Municipal Town Council or District Council": "(1) (a) In every financial year, there shall be paid to the Municipal City Council, a Municipal Town Council or a District Council a grant from the Consolidated Fund of an amount calculated according to such formula as may be prescribed. (b) The formula for the payment of grants under this section shall operate for such period and on such conditions as may be prescribed." This is the enabling statutory clause — a Consolidated-Fund grant per a prescribed formula — not a document naming a specific council or a dollar figure; Sections 84 ("Release of grants") and 85 ("Annual estimates") are companion provisions. Sections 132–133 ("Obligation to prepare financial statements" / "Contents and form of financial statements") separately require every local authority other than a Village Council to produce audited financial statements within 3 months of the financial year end, and are the statutory basis the Municipal City Council of Port Louis cites for its own annual report (see mu-portlouis-citycouncil-annualreport-2017-18).
targetReport.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument, currently in force per the Revised Laws version fetched.

results.basis: Acapulco's own Plan Municipal de Desarrollo Urbano opens its socio-demographic diagnosis by taking the municipality's population count directly from the 2020 census. Verbatim: "El Censo de Población y Vivienda del Instituto Nacional de Estadística, Geografía e Informática (INEGI) (2020) contabilizó una población de 779,566 habitantes en el municipio de Acapulco de Juárez, que representan el 22.0% de la población estatal". Independently corroborated by the Bienestar municipal profile for Acapulco de Juárez (https://www.gob.mx/cms/uploads/attachment/file/1061187/12001_AcapulcoDeJuarez_2026.pdf), whose footnotes carry the identical census citations. Additionally, pMDU section 4.5.3 (Población Económicamente Activa) — the section round 2 could see only in the table of contents — derives Acapulco's PEA, employed and unemployed counts from the 2020 census and INEGI's occupation tabulations. Verbatim: "Del Censo de Población y Vivienda (2020) y de los Tabulados de INEGI, se señala que para el municipio de Acapulco la PEA3 representa el 66% de la población total de más de 15 años; el 98% de la PEA corresponde a la población ocupada con 377,351 personas y el 2% a población desocupada corresponde a 7,626 acapulqueños". The section's Table 27 source line reads "Fuente: Elaboración propia CONURBA, 2021; con base en Tabulados de Ocupación, INEGI; Censo de Población y Vivienda INEGI, 2020".
