targetReport.title: Wet waardering onroerende zaken (Wet WOZ)
targetReport.description: The national law requiring every Dutch municipality to determine an annual market value ('WOZ-waarde') for every real-estate object in its territory, executed by the municipal college van burgemeester en wethouders. Functions in this corpus the way `esa-2010` or `sna-2008` do — a legally-established methodology standard other documents cite as their valuation basis, rather than a periodical release. VERIFIED DIRECTLY: wetten.overheid.nl BWBR0007119 downloaded and parsed for the operative articles.
targetReport.cadence_note: Art. 22 lid 2: the value fixed by a municipality's beschikking 'geldt voor een kalenderjaar' (applies for one calendar year) — an annual valuation cycle.

release_schedule.rule: Wet WOZ, artikel 24 lid 1: "De beschikking wordt genomen binnen acht weken na het begin van het kalenderjaar waarvoor zij geldt." (The WOZ-beschikking [property value assessment notice] must be issued within eight weeks after the start of the calendar year for which it applies.) Article 18 lid 2 sets the valuation reference date (waardepeildatum) as one year before the start of that calendar year.
release_schedule.note: The 2026-cycle deadline (8 weeks after 1 January 2026, i.e. ~26 February 2026) has already passed relative to today (2026-08-11), so the next occurrence shown is the 2027 cycle. In practice nearly all municipalities issue the WOZ-beschikking combined with the annual municipal tax bill (gemeentelijke belastingaanslag) before 1 March each year, consistent with this 8-week statutory deadline. No published multi-year calendar of exact dates exists; the date above is computed from the statutory rule, not read off a calendar.

targetReport.title: New Zealand Standard Industrial Output Classification (NZSIOC)
targetReport.description: The New Zealand-only output classification layered on top of ANZSIC 2006, and the level at which Stats NZ actually designs its business surveys and compiles the national accounts -- "NZSIOC is an output view of the ANZSIC classification designed for the production of aggregated industry statistics" (Stats NZ to the UN Committee of Experts on ISIC, 2022). Four hierarchical levels: Level 1, "16 categories at this level. They match with the ANZSIC division level, except for three categories which combine two divisions together"; Level 2, "31 categories at this level which generally match with the ANZSIC division level, except that agriculture and manufacturing are split"; Level 3, "55 categories at this level. This level generally matches an ANZSIC subdivision or consists of several smaller subdivisions combined together"; Level 4, "118 working industries" where the National Accounts are compiled. Stats NZ built it because ANZSIC 2006's structure "does not always mirror the New Zealand economy" -- specifically, "because of the significance of agriculture and its downstream industries, users require more information about agriculture and primary food product manufacturing than what is provided at the ANZSIC group level". TITLE VARIANT, on file so it is not rediscovered: Stats NZ's own 2010 implementation paper expands the acronym as "New Zealand Standard Industry Output Categories", while its 2022 and 2025 papers to UN classification bodies and the Annual Enterprise Survey's DataInfo+ metadata use "New Zealand Standard Industrial Output Classification". The later and more widely used form is taken as the title here. MINTED 2026-08-09 on Thomas's ruling, after a cheap-check pass established that NZSIOC has no defining publication of its own -- no edition, no catalogue number, no version -- and is distributed as downloadable classification tables. Three Stats NZ-authored sources describe it and none names a founding instrument; Stats NZ's 2022 UN paper says outright that NZSIOC "was created as an afterthought" whose "purpose and/or need was not actually considered during the ANZSIC06 review". The ruling was that `Research.1.md` sec.4's bar is named + titled, which NZSIOC meets, and that the volumes `anzsic` and `isic` happen to have were never a requirement.
targetReport.cadence_note: Evergreen; `releases_per_year` deliberately absent, per sec.4's one-off foundational-instrument shape and the precedent of `eu-reg-2016-2304`. There is no observed revision interval to derive a rate from: NZSIOC has no published edition sequence at all. Forward-looking caveat from Stats NZ's 2025 ECLAC workshop paper -- "There has been no review of ANZSIC since the commencement of the revision in 2006 and it is heavily out of date and difficult to use", and New Zealand is "contemplating adopting ISIC Rev 5 either as is or with a few minor class adjustments" -- so NZSIOC's parent may be replaced rather than revised, which would force a decision about this node rather than a routine update.

targetReport.description: The UN's standard classification for household consumption expenditure. Deliberately not minted for the Canada or US CPI slices already in the graph (`international-frameworks.json`'s own dropped notes: StatCan's CPI never uses COICOP at all, and BLS only produces a COICOP mapping as a side series for the OECD, not something the headline release rests on -- 'It should return if a document is found where COICOP governs a primary release.'). results.window:
I. Purpose and scope of the PCOICOP 
 The 2020 Philippine Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (PCOICOP) is a standard classification of individual consumption expenditures patterned after the 2018 Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) developed by the United Nations Statistics Division (UNSD) in 2018. The PCOICOP is used to identify individual consumption expenditures incurred by three institutional sectors of the 2008 System of National Accounts (SNA), namely: households, non-profit institutions serving households (NPISHs), and general government.

results.basis: PSA's PSIC classification page: "PSIC Revision 5 is patterned after the United Nations International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC) Revision 5, with modifications to reflect the country's economic structure."
results.evidenceQuote: PSIC Revision 5 is patterned after the United Nations International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC) Revision 5, with modifications to reflect the country's economic structure.

targetReport.title: International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC)
targetReport.description: The United Nations' industry classification and the acknowledged parent of most national industrial classifications, including ANZSIC and its two predecessors. Its absence from this corpus was a hole of the same shape as the missing `gasb-standards` that the associated-states pass had to fill: `naics` was present with eight inbound edges while the classification NAICS itself is aligned to was not represented at all. Adopted 1948; revisions 1 (1958), 2 (1968), 3 (1990), 3.1 (2002), 4 (2007) and 5 (endorsed 2023, publication forthcoming).
targetReport.cadence_note: Six revisions in seventy-five years. Rev. 5 was endorsed by the UN Statistical Commission at its 54th session in 2023 and, as of this session's read of the UNSD page, is 'forthcoming' in published form while being distributed as introduction, explanatory notes and structure files. releases_per_year is nominal.

release_schedule.note: ISIC has no publication calendar or fixed revision cycle. Revisions occur irregularly and infrequently (Rev.3: 1989, Rev.3.1: 2002, Rev.4: 2008, Rev.5: endorsed by the UN Statistical Commission at its 54th session in March 2023). National adaptation of Rev.5 is targeted by 2025, business register updates by 2026, and statistical program implementation from 2027, but these are implementation milestones for the already-published Rev.5, not a future release date. The UN Committee of Experts on International Statistical Classifications recommended a five-year revision cycle for ISIC/CPC (raised at the 55th Statistical Commission session, 2024), but as of the 56th session (2025) documents, this had not been formally adopted -- a new Standing Task Team on ISIC and CPC was instead tasked with developing a revision-cycle strategy proposal. No computable next revision date exists yet.

results.bestSpan: PSIC Revision 5 is patterned after the United Nations International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC) Revision 5, with modifications to reflect the country's economic structure.
results.window:
The Philippine Standard Industrial Classification (PSIC) is the country's official framework for classifying establishments and enterprises according to their primary economic activity. PSIC Revision 5 is patterned after the United Nations International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC) Revision 5, with modifications to reflect the country's economic structure, requirements, and evolving economic activities. The PSIC Revision 5 was developed to:
 1) respond to changes in economic activities, including the emergence of new industries and developments in existing industries; 
2) account for technological advancements that affect the organization of production and the shifting of economic activities; and 
3) maintain alignment with the latest ISIC revision to promote the international comparability of economic statistics.

results.evidenceQuote: The existing PSCC is patterned from the ASEAN Harmonized Tariff Nomenclature (AHTN) that is based on the Harmonized Commodity Description and Coding System (HS) issued by the World Customs Organization (WCO).

targetReport.title: Harmonized Commodity Description and Coding System (HS)
targetReport.description: The multipurpose international product nomenclature developed by the World Customs Organization: more than 5,000 commodity groups, each identified by a six-digit code. The commodity-side counterpart to the industry classifications already in this corpus — national trade statistics, including Canada's, are coded to it, with countries adding digits beyond six for tariff and statistical detail.
targetReport.cadence_note: The WCO's Harmonized System Committee 'prepares amendments updating the HS every 5 – 6 years' — editions 2002, 2007, 2012, 2017, 2022. Not an annual release; releases_per_year is nominal.

release_schedule.rule: The WCO prepares amendments updating the HS nomenclature every 5-6 years through the Review Sub-Committee and HS Committee; the HS Convention provides a two-and-one-half-year implementation period after adoption before a new edition enters into force (six months for reservations, two years for correlation tables/translation/legislative updates). The HS2022 edition entered into force 1 January 2022; the next edition, originally planned as HS2027, was pushed back one year due to COVID-19-related delays and will be HS2028, entering into force 1 January 2028.
release_schedule.note: This is a periodic amendment/nomenclature update, not a recurring data report with dated calendar entries. The WCO's own site frames it as a 5-6 year revision cycle governed by the HS Convention's implementation timeline rather than a fixed calendar. A further, more fundamental revision (HS2033) is already being planned as a follow-on cycle.

results.basis: The archived 2023-2025 version of the 'Indexing of Benefits' policy in the Alberta AISH policy manual (retained on the current Benefit Rate Adjustments page) states: 'AISH benefits are adjusted annually using the Alberta Consumer Price Index (CPI) starting on January 1, 2023 ... Annual benefit rate changes are calculated using the Alberta CPI (All-items, not seasonally adjusted). The Alberta CPI is published monthly by Statistics Canada and measures the change in price for goods and services bought by Albertans.' It sets out the formula X = A/B - 1, where A is the sum of the monthly Alberta CPI indexes for the 12 months ending September 30 before the adjustment date and B is the sum for the preceding 12 months. From January 1, 2026 the dependence on Alberta CPI is mediated by the Alberta escalator, which is capped at 2%.
results.evidenceQuote: How Benefits are Adjusted Annual benefit rate changes are calculated using the standard escalator amount established in the Alberta Personal Income Tax Act, which is the lesser of either two per cent, or the Alberta Consumer Price Index (CPI) amount from October through September year-over-year.

results.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A on Rosstat's own host. Приказ № 915 is the instrument that approves the official statistical methodology the CPI is computed under, in its own words: «Утвердить Официальную статистическую методологию наблюдения за потребительскими ценами на товары и услуги и расчета индексов потребительских цен (далее – Методология) (приложение № 1).» It supplies genuine method rather than a bare publication mandate -- it fixes the index formula («Расчет ИПЦ к предыдущему месяцу осуществляется в соответствии с модифицированной формулой Ласпейреса»), the observation cadence («ежемесячно по состоянию на конец месяца … еженедельно по состоянию на пятницу») and the weights basis («веса – мера относительной значимости товаров (услуг) в рамках сводного индекса цен, определяемая на основе потребительских расходов домашних хозяйств»). `methodology_depends_on` rather than `cites` on exactly the distinction `br-fiscal-responsibility-law.json` draws for `br-rreo -> br-lc-101-2000`: an instrument that defines the method the release relies on, not one that merely compels its publication.
results.evidenceQuote: Утвердить Официальную статистическую методологию наблюдения за потребительскими ценами на товары и услуги и расчета индексов потребительских цен (далее – Методология) (приложение № 1).

targetReport.title: Приказ Росстата от 15 декабря 2021 г. № 915 «Об утверждении Официальной статистической методологии наблюдения за потребительскими ценами на товары и услуги и расчета индексов потребительских цен»
targetReport.description: The standing Rosstat order approving the official statistical methodology behind the consumer price index -- the instrument BRICS/G.1 recorded as NOT FOUND. Its enabling clause establishes it as a standing instrument and, incidentally, supplies this round's independent corroboration that Постановление Правительства РФ № 420 of 2 June 2008 is the instrument constituting Rosstat: «В соответствии с подпунктом 5.2 Положения о Федеральной службе государственной статистики, утвержденного постановлением Правительства Российской Федерации от 2 июня 2008 г. № 420, п р и к а з ы в а ю: 1. Утвердить Официальную статистическую методологию наблюдения за потребительскими ценами на товары и услуги и расчета индексов потребительских цен (далее – Методология) (приложение № 1).» The observation cadence is fixed by the methodology itself, §5.2 «Периодичность и масштаб наблюдения» п.15: «Регистрация цен и тарифов осуществляется: по полному перечню товаров (услуг)-представителей, утвержденному соответствующим приказом Росстата, для расчета индекса потребительских цен – ежемесячно по состоянию на конец месяца (по установленному графику)… по сокращенному перечню товаров (услуг)-представителей, определенному соответствующим приказом Росстата – еженедельно по состоянию на пятницу.» The index formula is named explicitly: «Расчет ИПЦ к предыдущему месяцу осуществляется в соответствии с модифицированной формулой Ласпейреса» ("The CPI relative to the previous month is calculated in accordance with the modified Laspeyres formula"). The weights source is also named, and is an internal dependency this round could not follow to a node: «Для формирования Набора анализируются итоги выборочного обследования бюджетов домашних хозяйств, проводимого на территории всех субъектов Российской Федерации, в группировке Классификатора индивидуального потребления домашних хозяйств по целям (далее – КИПЦ-ДХ).» and «веса – мера относительной значимости товаров (услуг) в рамках сводного индекса цен, определяемая на основе потребительских расходов домашних хозяйств» -- the household budget survey itself was not separately located this round (see `_dropped`). Fetched TIER A from Rosstat's own host; the first attempt returned `curl: (35) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer`, which is Rosstat rate-limiting rather than a block, and succeeded on retry after a 6-second backoff.

release_schedule.note: No release calendar or stated periodicity exists. The Manual has been issued only three times: 1989 (ILO, 'Consumer Price Indices: An ILO Manual'), 2004 ('Consumer Price Index Manual: Theory and Practice'), and 2020 ('Consumer Price Index Manual: Concepts and Methods'), each ~15-16 years apart. The IMF's own page for this report is titled 'Update of the Consumer Price Index Manual' and explains the 2020 edition was produced because 'methods and best practices have continued to evolve' since 2004, following requests from the 2014 UNECE-ILO CPI Experts Meeting -- i.e., updates are triggered by inter-agency expert consensus, not a fixed schedule. No next-edition date or working-group timeline is published. This is consistent with the corpus's very low releases_per_year (0.06, i.e. roughly once per 16 years).

targetReport.title: Annual Survey of Manufacturing and Logging Industries (ASML)
targetReport.description: Annual census-and-sample survey of establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing and logging, IMDB record 2103. It is the annual anchor for the manufacturing side of the Canadian accounts and it names its own consumers in its own words: 'Within Statistics Canada, the data are used by the Canadian System of National Accounts, the Monthly Survey of Manufacturing (record number 2101) and Prices programs.' That sentence is the only present-tense statement of the ASML-to-MSM relationship found; the MSM's own record describes the arrangement in the past tense and dates it to 2003. Survey data are substituted with T1, T2, T3010 and T5013 tax data under the Integrated Business Statistics Program, which is an administrative input with no publication behind it. The IPPI's own record 2318 names the 2019 ASML as one of two weighting sources, which is why this node is worth more than a manufacturing statistic normally would be.

targetReport.title: Territorial Formula Financing
targetReport.description: The federal unconditional transfer to Yukon, the Northwest Territories and Nunavut that closes the gap between what a territory could raise on its own and what it needs to provide services comparable to those in the provinces, calculated under Part I.1 of the Federal-Provincial Fiscal Arrangements Act and Part 1.1 of SOR/2007-303. The fourth major federal transfer alongside the Canada Health Transfer, the Canada Social Transfer and Equalization, and until this entry the only one of the four with no node in this graph. Its revenue-base formula at s. 19 mirrors the DIVISION 2 Nova Scotia formula at s. 8 term for term in several places (SEPH, the System of Macroeconomic Accounts wage terms, Government Finance Statistics), which is what made this pass cheap once the equalization-named-products cluster had already verified the parallel citations.
targetReport.cadence_note: Entitlements are announced in December for the fiscal year beginning the following April 1, alongside Equalization, from the same certificate process.

entries.covers: TFF entitlements for fiscal year 2027-28 (beginning April 1, 2027)

release_schedule.rule: Federal-Provincial Fiscal Arrangements Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. F-8), s. 4.3: "The territorial formula financing payment payable to a territory for a fiscal year shall be calculated, at a time determined by the Minister, no later than three months before that fiscal year begins."
release_schedule.note: Statutory deadline is 3 months before the fiscal year starts (i.e., no later than Dec 31), but in practice Finance Canada has announced TFF and Equalization entitlements earlier in December each year via a joint news release: FY2022-23 announced Dec 16, 2021; FY2023-24 announced Dec 2022; FY2024-25 announced Dec 2023; FY2025-26 announced Dec 23, 2024. The next occurrence (for FY2027-28) is therefore expected around mid-to-late December 2026, with Dec 31, 2026 as the hard statutory backstop.

results.window:
「商品及服務輸出入」與「海關進出口」有何不同？ 答：
 商品及服務輸出入為本國常住居民(包括個人及機構)與非常住居民間商品所有權之移轉(包括買賣與贈與)以及本國常住居民對非常住居民提供(或接受)之服務。所稱商品及服務包括下列各類：
 (一)商品；
 (二)運輸服務；
 (三)維修服務；
 (四)保險服務；
 (五)什項商品與服務：
 (六)商品輸入(出)之調整；
 (七)非本國常住居民國內購買或本國常住居民國外購買；
 雖然商品輸出入統計之主要資料須以海關之貿易統計為依據，惟兩者定義、範圍略有不同，須加調整；其不同點主要為海關以商品之是否進關與出關為統計基礎，而國民所得統計則以所有權之移轉為計算基礎。另海關貿易統計對於出口商品價值係按離岸價值(F.O.B.)計算，進口商品則按到岸價值(C.I.F.)計算，而國民經濟會計對於輸入商品依C.I.F.價值離析為F.O.B.價值、本國常住居民對輸入商品提供承運及保險服務價值，與非本國常住居民對輸入商品提供承運及保險服務價值等三項，其中本國常住居民對輸入商品提供承運及保險價值因非屬服務輸入，故於服務輸出設置相應項目以為對減。另輸出除F.O.B.價值之商品，與服務輸入相應對減項目外，亦將本國常住居民提供之輸出承運及保險價值列計服務輸出。此外，一般稱海關商品進出口之差額為「出(入)超」，而國民所得統計之商品及服務輸出入之差額稱「順(逆)差」。 回上一頁

targetReport.title: Data Quality Assessment Framework (DQAF)
targetReport.description: The IMF's framework for structured assessment of statistical output quality, named as the explicit methodological basis of Tanzania's own CPI Data Quality Assessment: 'The IMF Data Quality Assessment Framework (DQAF) identifies quality-related features' (tz-nbs-cpi-dqa, Introduction, p.2). First minted this session -- a distinct node from imf-sdds and imf-e-gdds (dissemination-standard tiers) and from cpi-manual (compilation methodology): DQAF governs how quality itself is assessed and reported, not how the index is compiled or disseminated.
targetReport.cadence_note: A standing framework document, revised infrequently; not an annual release.

release_schedule.note: The DQAF is a methodological framework (a set of quality-assessment templates for statistical data categories), not a periodic statistical release. IMF's Statistics Department revises individual DQAF modules occasionally as needed (e.g., the original framework and supplement date to 2001-2003; the Public Sector Debt Statistics (PSDS) DQAF module was last dated August 2024) but there is no published release calendar or stated periodicity governing when revisions occur. The DSBB/DQRS portal hosts the current framework documents but shows no update schedule.

targetReport.title: Uganda National Household Survey 2016/2017 (UNHS VI)
targetReport.description: The sixth round of Uganda's National Household Survey, 'conducted from July 2016 to June 2017' (per the CPI release's own Foreword), whose expenditure data supply the weights currently used in the rebased Uganda CPI. A recurring, titled survey series (UNHS I-VI to date), the same node shape as Tanzania's Household Budget Survey and Kenya's rebasing-report weight source, minted here as its own node rather than folded into the CPI's description because it is independently named with its own round number and dates.
targetReport.cadence_note: Conducted roughly every 3 years; UNHS VI covered July 2016-June 2017.

release_schedule.note: UNHS VI (2016/17) is one specific past edition in a recurring UBOS survey series (UNHS), not itself a repeating publication. There is no published calendar or stated periodicity rule; UBOS has run rounds at irregular ~3-4 year intervals: 2016/17 (VI, report published 2018), 2019/20 (VII, report published 2021), 2023/24 (VIII, report released 15 May 2025 per https://www.ubos.org/uganda-national-household-survey-report-2023-2024-released/), and the 'Ninth Uganda National Household Survey (UNHS) 2026/2027' which was in enumerator-training/field-testing stage as of mid-July 2026 (https://nilepost.co.ug/news/356326/ubos-trains-80-data-collectors-ahead-of-20262027-national-household-survey, https://allafrica.com/stories/202607160614.html). No article specifies the fieldwork end date or report release date for this ninth round. Based on the observed lag between fiscal-year end and report release in the prior three rounds (roughly 10-14 months after the FY ends in June), the report for the 2026/2027 round is projected to appear in the first half of 2028; this projected date is an inference (implied), not a published date.

release_schedule.note: IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL CHANGE: this publication has moved from NHS England Digital to the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC), and been SPLIT into two separate annual publications on GOV.UK: 'Adult social care activity report, England' (https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/adult-social-care-activity-report-england-2024-to-2025) and 'Adult social care finance report, England' (https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/adult-social-care-finance-report-england-2024-to-2025). The NHS Digital landing page itself confirms: 'The Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) has taken responsibility for the publication of the Activity and Finance report' and it was divided into two separate publications. "The source of the figures in this release are the returns from local authorities in England to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG) in the Revenue Outturn (RO) forms." Also: "All local authorities in England are required to complete the Revenue Outturn (RO) suite of forms to show all transactions for the... financial year related to the general fund revenue account." targetReport.title: Revenue Outturn (RO) forms
targetReport.description: The standardised financial return every English local authority must complete annually, covering general fund revenue account transactions — the direct English counterpart to Alberta's Financial Information Return (FIR) and the Netherlands' Iv3-rapportage.
targetReport.cadence_note: Submitted in two stages per financial year: provisional figures (deadline late July) then certified figures (deadline mid-October), per MHCLG's technical notes.

release_schedule.note: MHCLG's annual letter to local authorities states: 'The RO 2025-26 return is due by Friday 24 July 2026' (provisional outturn, already passed as of today, 2026-08-11) and 'a certified return is emailed by Friday 9 October 2026'. This is an annual cycle: forms are distributed to English local authorities in April, provisional figures due late July, and a certified/final return due mid-October, each covering the financial year that ended the preceding March. Prior-year technical notes confirm the same pattern (2024-25 cycle: 'deadline for provisional RO figures was set for late July in 2025' and 'certified RO figures was set for mid-October'). The exact day (a specific Friday) shifts slightly year to year, so no single fixed rule sentence (e.g. 'by the fourth Friday of July') was found stated verbatim by the publisher; only year-specific letters give the exact dates. releases_per_year=1 on file is a reasonable simplification of what is really a two-stage (provisional + certified) annual return cycle for each financial year's data.

targetReport.description: The accounting standard every English local authority's Statement of Accounts must follow — the UK functional equivalent of `psab-psas` and the Netherlands' `nl-bbv`. targetReport.title: Small Area Income and Poverty Estimates (SAIPE)
targetReport.description: Annual model-based estimates of median household income and of the number and rate of people in poverty for every state and county, plus school-age (5-17) poverty counts for all 13,000+ school districts. It exists because direct survey estimates for small areas are too imprecise: SAIPE combines direct American Community Survey estimates with regression predictions built from IRS exemption counts, SNAP participation, population estimates, BEA personal income and prior decennial counts, using shrinkage estimation weighted by the reliability of the survey component. It is the operative statistical input to Title I education funding.

The most recent release (2024 SAIPE estimates) was published January 27, 2026 (https://www.census.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2026/2024-saipe.html), consistent with SAIPE being an annual release though the exact month has varied across years (Dec 2023, Dec 2024, Jan 2026).

SBV's Depository Corporations Survey DQAF metadata document (authored by SBV's Forecasting and Statistics Department) states: "The classification by institutional sectors is incomplete and not fully in line with the guidance of the IMF's Monetary and Financial Statistics Manual (MFSM)." and "With the implementation of International Accounting Standards (IAS) as the accounting and reporting framework for financial institutions in Vietnam, the SBV intends to gradually adapt the guidelines of the MFSM on (1) calculation of flows ...; (2) valuation of financial assets and liabilities; and (3) accrual accounting for the compilation of monetary and financial statistics." The citation names no edition and is paired elsewhere in the same document with '1993 SNA', which would normally point to the legacy MFSM (2000) rather than this corpus's versioned imf-mfsmcg-2016 node -- the same generic-citation-vs-versioned-node shape as the Iran/Iraq COICOP and Iran SNA-93 decisions.
